summary: mTLS SAN selection/ordering during client cert parse causes service-account impersonation 403s in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Several scheduled workers (service accounts) in the customer's private VPC are failing to authenticate to Redwood's admin API with 403 Forbidden errors. The customer is using mTLS client certs for service-account impersonation.

Observed behavior: After an ingress update rolled out a dependency bump to the certificate parsing library, some service certs that include multiple subjectAltName (SAN) entries are being parsed differently, resulting in Redwood extracting a different identity claim than expected. The wrong extracted identity does not map to the configured service account in the customer's RBAC, causing authorization failures for scheduled inference jobs.

Impact: Intermittent but frequent failures for background scheduled workers that use certificate-based service account impersonation. Customer reports increased job backlogs and missed SLAs for batch inference jobs. Affects Nimbus Analytics production pipelines in us-west-2.
impact: Multiple scheduled worker processes failing to authenticate (403) affecting nightly batch inference runs. Customer reported 22% job failure rate over past 24h and manual retries required. Business impact: delayed data delivery for customer SLAs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer uploads a PEM client certificate containing multiple SAN entries (e.g., DNS:nimbus-worker, URI:spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/worker).
2) Configure the service account mapping in Private RBAC to use the spiffe URI as the canonical principal.
3) Trigger a scheduled worker to call the admin-impersonation endpoint over mTLS.
4) Observe 403 Forbidden returned with authz checks showing principal mismatch in the auth logs.
logs: [2026-03-12T02:14:10Z] rbac-check: principal 'nimbus-worker' not bound to service-account 'batch-worker', rejecting with 403
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: change in cert parsing dependency altered SAN selection priority (DNS over URI) after an ingress dependency upgrade on 2026-03-11.
Reproduced in staging by installing the same ingress image and presenting a cert with multiple SAN types. Staging shows identical principal extraction behavior.
Confirmed that prior to the dependency bump the codebase selected the first URI SAN when present; the updated library surfaces DNSName first in the parsed list.
AuthN layer previously normalized to prefer spiffe URIs. New parsing order means the canonical principal becomes the DNS name unless we canonicalize explicitly.
Related past tickets: SUP-82109 (tenant-scoped-session-cookie prefixing) referenced for private RBAC mapping behaviors; SUP-412998 touches admin-impersonation 403s in private.
Customer provided certs and sample requests via secure upload (s3 link redacted).
comments: Samira Patel (Support): Received case from Nimbus complaining about scheduled jobs failing; escalated to infra on-call.

Liam O'Connor (SRE): I can reproduce in our staging cluster with the new ingress image. Looks like openssl/python-cryptography changed SAN ordering behavior in the dependency bump PR #482. Marking as In Progress.

Customer (Nimbus SRE): We started seeing intermittent failures immediately after your ingress update late on 2026-03-11. We can provide sample certs and timestamps.
Customer confirms they use URI SANs (spiffe) as canonical principal in RBAC config.
Avery Chen (Platform): Adding temporary workaround: we've created an ingress-side header injection to pass the spiffe SAN as X-Redwood-Principal when present; will test with customer.
Liam O'Connor (SRE): Deploying hotfix to staging to normalize SAN selection (prefer URI SANs when present) and to add logging around SAN selection to avoid silent mismatches.
root_cause: An upgrade to the ingress certificate-parsing dependency changed how subjectAltName entries are enumerated. The platform code relied on the previous enumeration order to find the spiffe URI SAN; the new parser returns DNSName entries first, leading to extracting the wrong identity string which does not match RBAC bindings.
resolution: Hotfix (rollout-branch): update ingress auth component to explicitly prefer and canonicalize URI SAN entries (spiffe) over DNS SANs when mapping to service-account principals. Added defensive fallback that scans all SAN entries for value matching a configured service account pattern. Rolled to staging on 2026-03-13 and to production (canary) on 2026-03-14 for the affected customer region us-west-2.
resolution_notes:
1) Hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/487
2) Canary in prod for Nimbus (us-west-2) shows successful authentication for previously failing jobs.
3) Post-deploy monitoring: 0% auth failures for Canary group over 4h; gradually expanded to 100% after 6h.
follow_up_actions: 1) Backport canonicalization and additional unit tests covering multiple SAN types to the supported ingress branches (release-2025.12, release-2026.01).
2) Add e2e test that presents certs with mixed SAN types and asserts principal mapping is deterministic and matches configured RBAC mappings.
3) Update runbook and Confluence page to document SAN precedence and recommended cert issuance patterns for customers using mTLS service accounts.
4) Notify affected customers via support banner and run a proactive scan for other private tenants with mixed-SAN certs in us-west-2.
5) Consider adding a configurable SAN precedence toggle for private deployments to accommodate customers with non-spiffe canonical principals.
